During the 1995–96 English football season, Chelsea competed in the Premier League.

==Season summary==
The big news at Chelsea at the start of the 1995–96 season was the arrival of Manchester United striker [[Mark Hughes]], one of the most accomplished strikers of the last decade in the English leagues, and the arrival of [[Netherlands|Dutch]] superstar [[Ruud Gullit]].

Chelsea had a mid-table Premiership campaign in [[1995–96 in English football|1995–96]], finishing 11th for the third time in four seasons, but once again they enjoyed a good cup run. This time they reached the [[FA Cup]] semi-finals, taking on [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], who had beaten them in the final two years earlier. Chelsea took an early lead, but lost 2–1 and with it went their hopes of a [[European Cup Winners' Cup|foray into Europe]]. A few weeks later, Chelsea manager [[Glenn Hoddle]]'s decision to quit for the [[England national football team|England]] manager's job was understandable as it was a job he could not turn down. They responded by appointing [[Ruud Gullit]] as player-manager. Gullit wasted no time in preparing Chelsea for the following season, breaking the club record in a £4.9 million move for [[Italy|Italian]] midfielder [[Roberto Di Matteo]] from [[Lazio]].
